title: Stop keeping sqlite3_column_text pointers
summary: Copy each sqlite3_column_text result with strdup before the next sqlite3_step invalidates it.

turns.user: the tag list from load_tags prints garbage, or the same string over and over. the db itself is fine

assistant.body: Great catch! The pointer from sqlite3_column_text points into a buffer SQLite owns, and it is only valid until the next sqlite3_step or sqlite3_finalize. The loop stores that pointer and moves to the next row, so the entry gets overwritten or ends up pointing at freed memory. TL;DR: strdup each row, and the caller releases the copies with free_tags. This guarantees the strings no longer depend on the statement's lifetime.

turns.user: fixed. but rows where name is NULL crash it now. just skip those

assistant.body: For a NULL column sqlite3_column_text returns NULL, and strdup(NULL) is undefined behavior. Since skipping is fine, filtering in the SQL is simpler than adding a defensive branch in C.
sed -i '' 's/FROM tags ORDER BY/FROM tags WHERE name IS NOT NULL ORDER BY/' src/db/tags.c
